sector_model: aerospace and industrial manufacturing (segment EBITDA, capex, receivable factoring, acquisitions, net debt); not a bank/insurer/REIT model
thesis: Howmet makes jet-engine components, fasteners, structures and forged wheels. Q3 2026 sales 2,703M (+29%), 9M sales 7,563M (+24%, includes CAM from 2026-04-06 and Brunner from 2026-02-06), operating income 9M 2,241M (includes 91M restructuring credits, mainly a 93M Savannah sale gain), net income 9M 1,681M, OCF 1,745M, capex 345M. Engine Products Q3 segment EBITDA margin 39.1% vs 33.3%. Investment grade (BBB+/Baa1 positive/A-), 5,000M added to buyback authorization 2026-10-28. At the verified 2026-11-09 close 216.24 and 397.66M shares the market cap is about 86.0B: 41.8x TTM GAAP net income, 2.2% TTM FCF yield, which prices in several more years of aerospace and gas-turbine growth at high margins. Business quality looks high; the price looks demanding, so this is a quality-at-a-full-price watch, not a bargain.
counterthesis: 41.8x TTM earnings (about 43x excluding the 91M gain, before tax effect) and a 2.2% FCF yield leave little room for a slowdown in aircraft builds, engine spares or gas turbines. Part of the 24% growth is acquired (CAM, Brunner) and part is aluminum and inflation cost pass-through, so organic growth is lower than headline. OCF is helped by receivable sales without recourse (1,069M in 9M26 under one program plus 1,043M under customer programs, presented in operating cash flow) and by deferred revenue growth. Net debt rose to about 3.9B after the 1.9B of acquisitions, 1.1B of buybacks were done at 230-265 per share, and a 300M 6.75% bond is due Jan 2028. Concentration in commercial aerospace (aircraft and engine OEM demand) and tariff, supplier and headcount absorption risks (about 520 net hires in Engine Products in Q3) are unquantified here.
invalidation: Commercial aerospace build rates or engine spares falling, Engine Products EBITDA margin rolling back below about 35%, organic growth falling to single digits while the stock still trades above 40x earnings, FCF conversion dropping because receivable sales are curtailed, or debt-funded acquisitions and buybacks pushing leverage up.
